metadata.title: AAPL Stock Unmoved After-Hours — Apple Sues OpenAI Over Alleged 'Rotten' Campaign To Steal AI Hardware Secrets

content.text:
AAPL Stock Unmoved After-Hours — Apple Sues OpenAI Over Alleged 'Rotten' Campaign To Steal AI Hardware Secrets
-
Apple alleges OpenAI pushed departing employees to download secret files, blueprints, and prototypes to help build its own upcoming AI hardware.
-
The lawsuit highlights OpenAI's hardware chief, Tang Tan, and a former engineer, Chang Liu, accusing them of using insider access to steal information.
-
The legal battle marks a major split between the two tech giants, who previously partnered to put ChatGPT features into Apple's Siri.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) has sued OpenAI in a federal court in California, alleging that the artificial intelligence company orchestrated a widespread effort to steal trade secrets and hardware designs.
The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI encouraged current and former Apple workers to hand over confidential documents, blueprints, and physical components. Apple claims this misconduct was guided by OpenAI's leadership to jump-start its own competing AI devices.
"At every level, from members of its technical staff to its chief hardware officer, and in coordination with business partners, OpenAI has been stealing Apple's trade secrets and confidential information," the Cupertino, California-based tech giant said in the suit. "As a natural result, OpenAI's nascent hardware business now rests on the shakiest of foundations, rotten to its core by its illegal reliance on misappropriated trade secrets."
AAPL stock was flat after-hours at the time of writing. The stock eased on Friday but recorded its second consecutive week of gains.
Former Executives Accused
The lawsuit focuses heavily on Tang Tan, OpenAI's chief hardware officer. Tan previously worked at Apple for 24 years, serving as vice president of product design for the iPhone and Apple Watch. Apple claims Tan met with OpenAI months before leaving his job in early 2024 and shared secret details about Apple's suppliers.
According to the suit, Tan and OpenAI later asked Apple job candidates to bring secret digital designs and prototypes to interviews for "show and tell sessions". More than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI, including a top executive who left last month to lead its smart-glasses efforts.
The complaint also names Chang Liu, a former Apple electrical engineer who joined OpenAI in January. Apple claims Liu downloaded dozens of sensitive files about unreleased products. The lawsuit says Liu used a friend's Apple computer to bypass security and later exploited a system flaw to access files after he quit, texting his friend: "LOL, I found out I can access the [network storage], so funny."
